description: Find where a word, number or phrase appears in one document without reading it: use it instead of reading a long document whole, and instead of shelling out to pdftotext or grep. Takes a local `path` (same formats as distill_file) or a `url` (same as distill_url); the document is converted once and the cached Markdown is searched. Matching is case-insensitive, ignores line wraps and extra whitespace, and finds numbers split across lines; set `regex` for a JavaScript regular expression (at most 200 characters; a regex that runs longer than 2 s is stopped with bad_request). Each hit has the line, the physical page number (1-based position in the PDF, not the printed label; absent for documents without pages), the nearest heading above it and a few lines of context; neighbouring matches are merged into one hit. Next step after a hit: read around it with distill_file using `section` (the hit's heading) or `offset`/`limit` (from the hit's line), or look at the original page with distill_page_image. Read-only: never modifies or uploads anything. A `path` stays on this machine; only a `url` reaches the internet (public pages only, with the safety rules of distill_url), which is why the tool is marked as open-world. Fails like distill_file or distill_url (password_protected, needs_libreoffice, forbidden, too_large over 100 MB for documents, 2 GB for audio and video, parse_failed, fetch_failed) or with bad_request (neither or both of path and url, an invalid or over-long regex, or one using lookarounds or backreferences).

context.description: Lines of context before and after each match (default 2)

maxHits.description: Maximum number of hits to return (default 20); total says how many there are

path.description: Absolute path, or relative to the server's working directory. Pass either path or url

query.description: Text to find. Plain text by default: case-insensitive, whitespace-insensitive, matches across line wraps

regex.description: Treat query as an RE2 regular expression (case-insensitive, at most 200 characters; JavaScript-like syntax but no lookarounds or backreferences, always linear time)

url.description: Absolute http or https URL of a page. Pass either path or url

name: distill_search
title: Search inside a document
